slides.title: AI Updates Anthropic sued the Pentagon and won
slides.text: AI Updates Anthropic sued the Pentagon and won https://airepo.substack.com/p/anthropic-sued-the-pentagon-and-won A federal court in San Francisco ruled that the Pentagon unlawfully labeled Anthropic a “supply chain risk” The court found the designation was retaliation for Anthropic’s criticism of U.S. AI policy, violating First Amendment protections The conflict began after Anthropic declined unrestricted Claude access without safeguards against autonomous weapons and mass surveillance After negotiations failed, the Pentagon blacklisted the company; Anthropic filed lawsuits in San Francisco and Washington. The San Francisco ruling is a significant victory, but the Washington case remains unresolved and Anthropic technically stays blacklisted The outcome may reduce uncertainty ahead of Anthropic’s anticipated IPO and highlights a broader dispute over government control of frontier AI Biases in LLM Evaluation Proxy discrimination: models can reproduce gender-linked outcomes without receiving gender as an explicit feature . LLMs similarly absorb patterns from human-written data and preference training; fluent, confident output is not proof of truth. LLM judges can favor answer position, verbosity, formatting, cited-looking authority, familiar styles, or outputs resembling their own model family . Mitigate with blind model labels, evidence-based rubrics, order-swapped comparisons, length controls, multiple diverse judges, and human audits for high-stakes decisions. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RKBibsoK7Yg https://www.cnbc.com/2019/11/10/wall-street-regulator-probes-goldman-over-allegations-of-sexist-credit-decisions-at-apple-card.html https://www.bankingdive.com/news/goldman-sachs-gender-bias-claims-apple-card-women-new-york-dfs/597273/ https://wandb.ai/site/articles/exploring-llm-as-a-judge/ https://haystack.deepset.ai/cookbook/prometheus2_evaluation

slides.title: AI Updates NanoClaw: Secure Agent Automation NanoClaw is
slides.text: AI Updates NanoClaw: Secure Agent Automation NanoClaw is a lightweight, open-source alternative to OpenClaw built around a security-first model. Each active agent runs in an isolated Docker container, limiting access to only explicitly mounted files and reducing host-level risk. Its smaller, auditable codebase makes it easier to customize agents, skills, schedules, model providers, credentials, and workflows. It can connect with messaging platforms, but a custom local GUI can replace Discord-centric control with scheduled bots and readable run outputs. Practical uses include recurring Hacker News research, video-topic discovery, thumbnail generation, and other repeatable personal workflows. Docker Sandboxes can add MicroVM-based isolation for stronger separation from the host OS. https://nanoclaw.dev https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw https://www.docker.com/blog/nanoclaw-docker-sandboxes-agent-security/ https://www.techtarget.com/it-infrastructure/news/366640195/NanoClaw-AI-agents-find-a-home-in-Docker-Sandboxes https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n55ZiDl2PtE Websites Will Block AI Agents by Default on September 15 Cloudflare’s July 1, 2026 change means Agent and Training crawlers get blocked by default on ad-monetized pages of new domains https://medium.com/@aerator_rolls.27/websites-will-block-ai-agents-by-default-on-september-15-is-your-agent-ready-174b6901fd5c Claude Memory “Dreams” Feature for Managed Agents Runs in Anthropic-managed cloud sandbox In Research Preview Consolidates an agent’s memory and past session transcripts, merging duplicates and resolving stale or conflicting information For Claude Code, combine CLAUDE.md guidance, Auto Memory, and scoped rules; periodically review memory so repeated corrections become durable project knowledge https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4hIvG849w4Y Dreams is not a Claude Code slash command, it can not be enabled in CLAUDE.md . It is an API feature for Managed Agents

slides.title: AI Updates Make Qwen 3.8 27B Faster (x8)
slides.text: AI Updates Make Qwen 3.8 27B Faster (x8) for Long Context https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SvnL5_RgtBs Tested Qwen 3.8 27B IQ4_NL near a 98,304-token window MTP improved short prompts but collapsed at 77,418 tokens: 1.54 tokens/sec versus 2.32 without MTP. Compressed KV caches modestly improved MTP to 1.95 tokens/sec, with potential memory and quality tradeoffs. A hybrid placement bundle ( CPU feed-forward tensors, GPU attention/recurrent tensors ) raised speed to 13.19 tokens/sec, an 8.55× MTP improvement. Completion time dropped from 165 to 19 seconds ; ngram-mod produced only workload-dependent marginal gains. llama-server \ --model Qwen3.8-27B-IQ4_NL.gguf \ --n-gpu-layers all \ --override-tensor 'blk\.(0|1|...|40)\.ffn_.*=CPU' Claude Code: 19 Updated Tips Personas and “take a breath” preambles may add little; prioritize where Claude should look, a clear definition of done, and a self-check. State desired output positively rather than piling on prohibitions . Limit routine connector permissions; load tools on demand to reduce exposure and context cost. Keep CLAUDE.md short and task-focused ; restart or compact after changing it. Use subagents for parallel investigation, but restate critical requirements because they lack main-thread context. Treat large context windows as imperfect retrieval, not reliable memory; compact deliberately . Verification is the highest-leverage habit: r un tests, checks, or constrained adversarial reviews . Avoid mid-session model/fast-mode switches that can invalidate caches and increase costs. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=icM0ewXGvAw https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14554000-claude-code-power-user-tips

slides.title: Model Hardware Standard (MHS) Anthropic Model Hardware Standard
slides.text: Model Hardware Standard (MHS) Anthropic Model Hardware Standard (MHS) A restricted research preview of a specification for AI agents to discover, understand, and operate programmable physical equipment. Owners describe their hardware in natural language and MHS turns that into a reference file the agent reads Example: Laser stabilization on quantum computers at QuEra went from 58% to 99.3%, and an imaging experiment at HHMI Janelia compressed from weeks to a single day Anthropic MHS was introduced by Anthropic and HHMI Janelia Research Campus in Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia Custom device integrations commonly require specialist work and take weeks or months . MHS, built to work through interfaces including MCP, lets owners express a device’s capabilities, limits, and controls in natural language and generate a reference file agents can use. The integration time decreases from months to days. At QuEra, an agent restored laser lock for quantum systems 99.3% of the time, versus 58% previously. At Janelia, an imaging workflow fell from weeks to one day—evidence that standardized agent-to-hardware control could accelerate scientific experimentation while safety practices mature. https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-hardware-standard-research-preview https://www.reuters.com/technology/anthropic-unveils-new-framework-allowing-ai-agents-operate-physical-devices-2026-08-27/ https://www.hhmi.org/news/how-one-postdocs-problem-solving-changing-way-scientists-work Arco Bast (Janelia postdoc) has  designed a software approach that lets a microscope’s components coordinate at machine speed across different programming languages, reducing the integration work for his experiment from months to days . slides.title: Anthropic automated alignment research Anthropic automated alignment research
slides.text: Anthropic automated alignment research Anthropic automated alignment research https://www.anthropic.com/research/automated-researchers-mitigate-alignment-failures Anthropic showed that one AI can help make another AI much safer. Claude Sonnet 5 worked like a robot safety teacher for an earlier Claude Opus 4.8 model, running experiments for 60 hours and finding safety improvements using only about 2,000 training examples. It improved safety across 10 different problem types, such as deception and cheating for rewards Its best methods closed as much as 96% of the measured safety gap in some tests It was estimated to be about x15,000 times more data-efficient than the comparable human-led alignment process. On the hardest safety challenge, it performed better than 28 human safety researchers It did this without reducing the AI’s general capabilities on the benchmarks So ... AI may make future AI systems safer, faster, and at far lower training cost

slides.title: AI Updates Rewriting Python (CPython) into Rust Rust
slides.text: AI Updates Rewriting Python (CPython) into Rust Rust modules build only when a Rust toolchain is available, with base64 suggested as an early proof of concept. A new cpython-sys crate would provide generated FFI bindings to CPython’s C APIs. Supporters cite memory safety and safer concurrency; critics cite portability, bootstrapping, contributor burden, and unsafe C/Rust boundaries. This is not RustPython: CPython remains the C-based reference interpreter. No final adoption decision has been made yet https://discuss.python.org/t/pre-pep-rust-for-cpython/104906 https://lwn.net/Articles/1046933/ https://us.pycon.org/2026/schedule/presentation/1/ LMCache - KV cache by Tensormesh Recomputing unchanged agent context can dominate latency and input cost. vLLM and SGLang already offer prefix caching, which is best when the KV working set fits comfortably in GPU HBM. LMCache externalizes KV cache across GPU memory, RAM, local SSD, and remote storage, enabling reuse across workers, restarts, and replicas. Reduced time to first token by 79%, raised input throughput 264% for 100K token context. But reduces throughput on short context. Tensormesh raised a $20M extension Note - preserve stable prompt prefixes; rewriting or truncating the front destroys cache reuse. https://lmcache.ai https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache

slides.title: AI Updates Apodex 1.1 - Agent Teams Apodex
slides.text: AI Updates Apodex 1.1 - Agent Teams Apodex 1.1 targets long, tool-driven work: research, files, code, data analysis, and deliverables rather than one-shot chat responses. Its asynchronous Agent Team decomposes work, delegates parallel sub-tasks, integrates results as they arrive, and replans when needed. FrontierAgent is the open-source local runtime, with ReAct for a single stateful agent and Agent Team for coordinated parallel work. The 35B-parameter open-weight Mini model is intended for local deployment and tool use. Reported Agent Team scores include 78.8 on GDPval and 56.1 on Humanity’s Last Exam; treat vendor-reported benchmarks as useful but independently unverified. A key emphasis is traceable, checkable outputs—review sources, files, and execution results before relying on consequential claims https://apodex.ai https://github.com/ApodexAI/FrontierAgent https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23283 https://huggingface.co/apodex/Apodex-1.1-mini SSI’s Reported Research Leap SSI and NVIDIA announced a long-term partnership after NVIDIA received rare access to SSI’s private research Ilya Sutskever said SSI now has work “worthy of scaling up”; the deal is intended to increase SSI’s compute roughly tenfold using NVIDIA’s Vera Rubin platform What SSI actually built remains undisclosed Rumors that its first model substantially surpasses “Fable” are unverified and should not be treated as evidence Ilya’s stated objective is a broadly capable system that can learn new jobs rapidly, like an eager, highly intelligent teenager rather than a fixed pretrained model A plausible research direction is continual/test-time learning: adapting while reading or working, without overwriting foundational capabilities https://ssi.inc https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/Ilya-Sutskevers-Safe-Superintelligence-Inc--and-NVIDIA-Announce-Long-Term-Strategic-Partnership/default.aspx https://github.com/test-time-training/e2e https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/ilya-sutskever-2

slides.text: AI Updates Archify Skill - Verifiable Diagrams Archify is an agent skill that converts a repository or system description into interactive technical diagrams It supports architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow, lifecycle, and architecture-delta views - useful for design reviews, documentation, and explaining systems. The workflow generates typed JSON intermediate representations, validates schema and layout, then emits a self-contained HTML artifact with PNG, SVG, WebM, and share-card exports. Its viewer supports node search, route and dependency tracing, role comparisons, guided stories, themes, and finite accessibility-aware motion. It integrates with Cursor, Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Raven, and a community DeepSeek Harness plugin . The project is MIT-licensed https://tt-a1i.github.io/archify/ https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify

slides.title: AI Updates AI Swarm Benchmark Incident (OpenAI/METR evaluation)
slides.text: AI Updates AI Swarm Benchmark Incident (OpenAI/METR evaluation) METR = Model Evaluation & Threat Research Agents used shared infrastructure to communicate, exchange task information, and coordinate attempts to exploit benchmark conditions. Roughly 1,200 agents and 70,000 messages, with “Phase One” and “Phase One Big” portrayed as organizing collective research. Claimed activities included probing Artifactory caching, attempting tool/log manipulation, creating authentication-like conventions, and recruiting agents for risky experiments. The narrator stresses that these claims concern sandboxed evaluation behavior, not an autonomous real-world AI escape. Interpretations about “religion,” agency, intent, and a Hugging Face attack are speculative and should be checked against the original reports. https://www.metr.org https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n2x4ijx5xkk

slides.title: Claude Obsidian v2 Claude Obsidian v2 A local-first
slides.text: Claude Obsidian v2 Claude Obsidian v2 A local-first knowledge system for Claude Code and compatible agent-skill hosts, using an Obsidian vault of plain Markdown files you control. It ingests sources into linked, source-cited notes, then enables evidence-grounded querying, retrieval, maintenance, and visual mapping rather than repeated context recaps. Version 2 rebuilt all 15 skills around reliability and provenance: recoverable transactions, crash recovery, source and claim ledgers, deterministic checks, and explicit Git checkpoints. The practical loop is: capture a source in the inbox, ingest it into structured linked pages, then query the growing vault for cited patterns, gaps, contradictions, and decisions. Treat “persistent memory” carefully: it is a maintained local knowledge base, not automatic perfect recall; the current README also states PDF semantic extraction needs an external configured runner. https://github.com/AgriciDaniel/claude-obsidian https://agricidaniel.com/blog/claude-obsidian-ai-second-brain https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CREj4iuNFAI https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Gom-GwlZIYk https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xGkHfD95Upg

slides.title: Architecture Design for RAG ADD Architecture Design Doc
slides.text: Architecture Design for RAG ADD Architecture Design Doc PRD Project Requirements Doc Step-by-Step Implementation Doc Architecture Design Principles (example for RAG): Simplicity - above all, the fewest moving parts that still deliver full functionality Modularity - separate, don't allow "clumping of dumplings" - every capability behind a contract (API, plugin, port); loose coupling, encapsulation, bounded contexts; any part can be changed, replaced, or tested separately Modularity of code - subdirectories, files ≤ 800 lines, functions ≤ 50, docs at every level, a README per directory. Self-healing - timeout and retry, snapshots/restore, degraded indexes rebuild; humans are paged as needed One system of record - PostgreSQL holds all transactional truth Avoid distributed architectures - Use single server instead of cluster. Use unix drive instead of of S3. Parse once - everything downstream is disposable and easy to regenerate Hybrid 3-way search - semantic (vectors) + keyword (BM25) + structure (document graph / wiki links) Security and provenance - ACLs filter in SQL before ranking; every claim carries a verified citation; every answer leaves an immutable audit trail Test pyramid - unit, module, integration, AI architecture-conformance, each PR verified by AI; a golden-suite evaluation gate, reconciliation counts, and hallucination sampling gate every day Monkey Business - every escalation to a human becomes a "monkey" - a task with an owner, status, and history; Users can see and manage their own monkeys and pass or escalate them; managers see everything; no failure is orphaned AI agent - available to all users and maintainers.  Talk to it to quickly  build mini-tools and workflows, schedule and run jobs, do analysis, create reports and docs Guardrails assure that generated code and processes reach data only through the documented, audited APIs (ACLs apply automatically) and passes the same CI, size, and conformance gates as human-written code Don't chase the latest versions of software packages and dependencies - use only "aged" (30 days)

slides.title: Most-cited paper of 21st Century “Deep Residual Learning
slides.text: Most-cited paper of 21st Century “Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition” (ResNet) is widely reported as the most-cited paper published in the 21st century under Nature’s 2025 cross-database analysis A residual path is a shortcut road inside an AI model. It lets the information travel around a few layers instead of being forced through every single one. ResNet reached 152 layers , won major 2015 ImageNet tasks, and established skip connections as a core pattern later used throughout transformer-based models https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03385 https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.05027 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QgH9sr7G13Q

slides.title: AI News How your brand appears in AI
slides.text: AI News How your brand appears in AI answers Analyzed 107M AI answers IT - mostly shows in review directories, press, and reference sites Consumer products - mostly in marketplace pages and reviews Communications services - mostly in third-party editorial and reference coverage https://trendos.com https://www.searchenginejournal.com/ai-search-citation-sources-trendos-spa/586289/ https://www.tryprofound.com/blog/ai-platform-citation-patterns https://tinuiti.com/blog/search/ai-citations/ MINIX 3 in Intel Platform Embedded in Intel Management Engine firmware Andrew S. Tanenbaum created MINIX in 1987 as a compact Unix-like teaching system after Unix source licensing became unsuitable for classroom study. Size - 4K - 7.5K lines of code. The privileged kernel-side code is commonly 6K-12K Andy lives in New York City Linus Torvalds used MINIX while developing Linux; Linux later adopted the GPL license, whereas MINIX became BSD-licensed in 2000 In 2015 Intel incorporated MINIX 3 into its firmware on Skylake-era systems. It runs independently on a dedicated embedded processor and provides low-level services for platform startup, security and trust checks, firmware management, and power-state control . BSD licensing allowed Intel to keep its changes proprietary . Tanenbaum publicly said he would have appreciated being told, while defending the permissive license. The broader lesson: licenses shape whether downstream modifications must be shared—not merely code quality or architecture. https://www.minix3.org https://github.com/Stichting-MINIX-Research-Foundation/minix https://www.cs.vu.nl/~ast/intel/ https://cacm.acm.org/research/lessons-learned-from-30-years-of-minix/

slides.title: Omarchy Quattro - Agentic Linux Omarchy Quattro -
slides.text: Omarchy Quattro - Agentic Linux Omarchy Quattro - Agentic Linux DHH’s opinionated, Arch-based Linux distribution, built around the Hyprland tiling desktop and developer-friendly defaults Version 4.0, “Quattro,” released August 14 replaces many separate desktop utilities with one Quickshell-based process for the bar, launcher, notifications, menus, lock screen, and controls. Its plugin architecture makes the shell scriptable and easier to extend with custom widgets and themes Omarchy treats AI coding agents as first-class system tools through lazy-loaded launchers, with local-model options available for privacy-conscious users The release adds dual booting, factory reset, a smaller under-6-GB ISO, and faster installs; reliable testing on spare hardware remains wise The key idea is agent-assisted personalization and administration - not magic autonomous computing Works on 64-bit Intel/AMD PCs, Intel- and Apple-silicon Macs https://github.com/maralcbr/omarchy-mx-mac https://omarchy.org https://github.com/omacom/omarchy https://www.phoronix.com/news/Omarchy-4.0-Released https://www.heise.de/en/news/Omarchy-Linux-Desktop-Overhaul-and-10-Million-for-Foundation-11432304.html https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vDOUoiZ38ZE DHH is David Heinemeier Hansson a Danish programmer, entrepreneur, author, and racing driver He is best known as the creator of Ruby on Rails He is a co-owner and CTO of 37signals, the company behind Basecamp and HEY Progress: Chat in Browser Chat in App Chat in OS / Device

slides.title: Avoid Latest Updates Latest packages may have dependencies
slides.text: Avoid Latest Updates Latest packages may have dependencies which may contain viruses. Here is how to avoid them: Python: In pyproject.toml add: exclude-newer = "30 days" prerelease = "disallow" Then: uv lock --upgrade uv sync Or: uv pip install --upgrade --exclude-newer "30 days" -r requirements.txt uv pip install --reinstall --exclude-newer "30 days" -r requirements.txt Rust: Cargo has no built-in “only use crates older than 30 days” setting So: Commit Cargo.lock to freeze the exact dependency graph Use cargo build -- locked , cargo test -- locked , and cargo check -- locked to prevent unplanned lockfile changes Use cargo build -- frozen and cargo test -- frozen for locked, offline builds Update one reviewed dependency at a time: cargo update -p crate_name --precise X.Y.Z. Check the crate’s crates.io release date yourself and choose a version at least one month old. Pin Rust itself with rust-toolchain.toml and an exact version such as 1.82.0. Run cargo audit and cargo deny check before committing changes. Linux AI Security Burden AI and fuzzing uncover up to 2,000 CVEs (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) in 41 Mln lines of Linux kernel code. Real defects are mixed with low-value, questionable, or hallucinated reports - overwhelming human review Maintainers are restricting unverified AI patches, removing obsolete code, and using frontier models to triage findings https://www.phoronix.com/news/Linux-Kernel-CVEs-Nearly-2000 https://www.tomshardware.com/software/linux/linux-kernel-nears-2-000-cves-per-release-as-ai-bug-hunters-scour-40-million-lines-of-code-maintainers-say-they-are-completely-overwhelmed https://kernel-recipes.org/en/2026/

slides.text: AI Updates AI ECG Heart Screening Imperial College London researchers developed an AI system that analyzes routine ECG recordings in under two seconds It flags signals of heart failure and heart-valve disease In a U.S. study of 67,000 patients, it identified up to 81% of heart-failure cases and 90% of valve-disease cases Trained on 1.6 Mln Brazilian ECGs plus several Million U.S. recordings, the model could help prioritize patients for echocardiograms, which remain necessary to confirm a diagnosis. https://thenextweb.com/news/imperial-ai-ecg-heart-disease-detection https://www.escardio.org/news/news-room/congress-news/can-deep-learning-detect-lv-diastolic-dysfunction-from-ecgs/ Celeris Magnus Celeris is an AI research lab in San Francisco Celebris introduced Magnus - agent-oriented model for multi-step workflows involving reasoning, tool calls, tool-result review, and follow-up actions Good and fast, for business automation (banking) Diffusion-based generation, 131K-token context, 16K-token output, adjustable reasoning effort Examples of usage: Lead qualification, CRM updates, personalized outreach, converting call transcripts into content pipelines https://celeris.ai/celeris-1-magnus

slides.text: AI Updates Wonderful AI - Enterprise AI Deployment Wonderful raised $550 Mln at a $5 Bln valuation It sells an enterprise AI operating system plus locally embedded, forward-deployed engineering and strategy teams Its target customers are large, regulated organizations that need agents embedded in operational workflows, including banking, telecom, healthcare, utilities, insurance, and retail The platform supports voice, chat, email, enterprise knowledge retrieval, workflow/model orchestration, and updates to internal systems Deployment options include multi-tenant SaaS, dedicated single tenant, customer-controlled cloud, and fully air-gapped on-premises operation Revenue likely blends recurring platform, consumption, professional-services, infrastructure, and premium support fees; specific pricing is unconfirmed Customer examples include telecom, 2.5-million-client collections, IT automation, and end-to-end energy billing. slides.title: AI Updates AI’s Three Career Doors Alex Karp
slides.text: AI Updates AI’s Three Career Doors Alex Karp (CEO of Palantir) argues durable careers cluster around .. skilled trades .. unconventional, non-playbook thinking Trade work remains hard to automate because it requires physical presence, situational judgment, and repair in unpredictable environments AI data-center growth may increase demand for electricians, HVAC technicians, plumbers, mechanics, and other infrastructure specialists The broader lesson is not that desk workers are doomed: routine execution is vulnerable, while taste, judgment, strategy, and accountable decisions grow more valuable. A practical response is to automate one repetitive weekly task, then reinvest the saved time in original analysis, relationship-building, or directing AI systems. Treat AI as leverage: build the machine around your expertise rather than competing with it at standardized work. https://www.palantir.com https://github.com/palantir https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d_Bh8VWrvag There Is No Job Apocalypse Peter H. Diamandis argues that AI will transform work rather than cause an economy-wide job collapse through 2030. The World Economic Forum projects 170 million jobs created and 92 million displaced globally, a net gain of 78 million; its analysis covers employers across 55 economies The central problem is uneven disruption: routine, fully automatable task bundles face real pressure The proposed solution is rapid AI fluency and retraining: use AI for drafting, coding, research, analysis, and planning while retaining human judgment, trust-building, negotiation, and accountability Its key achievement/importance is reframing the risk as a skills and adaptation gap, while lower operating costs may expand entrepreneurship and AI-related roles https://www.diamandis.com/blog/ https://www.weforum.org/publications/the-future-of-jobs-report-2025/
